amendmentA3.readFrom: captain head 913410b1c; the determination file at my base carries only amendment and amendment2.
amendmentA3.appliedTo: every fee, service and filing-destination finding in all five rows.
amendmentA3.whatItConfirmed: The West Virginia repair's refusal to take its number from the compiled state profile was not merely defensible but required, and I can name the trap it avoided. The same WV profile carries, three times over, 'For 61-11-25 acquittal/dismissal/diversion/deferred-adjudication expungement, no filing fees or costs are charged' and 'Fee rule: no filing fees or costs are charged for a 61-11-25 action.' Section 61-11-25 is not § 61-11-26. A repairer treating that profile as one held document — which A2 read literally licensed — could have published 'no filing fee' for a petition that in fact costs $200. That is the California 1203.4 trap with the sign flipped and the stakes higher: a participant told filing is free, arriving at the circuit clerk's counter owing $200. Read per fact, the profile's own § 61-11-26 line does address this route and establishes the $100 State Police fee plus a numberless cross-reference to the civil-action fee, so it is silent on the figure rather than wrong about it; the $200 comes from the track registry, the route census and the packet-set manifest, each keyed to this track, this route key and this packet set respectively.
amendmentA3.whatItAlsoDid: Confirmed the Arkansas fee PASS as route-addressing — the AR feeRules list is flat and jurisdiction-wide, but every line in it gives the same answer and attributes it to the same Act 1460 this route's petition is captioned to, so there is no competing statutory section and no wrong line available to pick — and strengthened two Arkansas failures with further route-addressing facts the profile holds (the file-in-each-county rule, and a 30-or-90-day objection window by offence class).

theOpenCounselQuestionIWasAskedToRecordN.question: Whether relief under W. Va. Code § 17C-5-2b (and § 60A-4-407) counts against the once-per-lifetime limit in § 61-11-26(o).
theOpenCounselQuestionIWasAskedToRecordN.whereItLives: data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json, on the shared node wv_common_conv_procedure, 'Shared Conviction Expungement Procedure, Exclusion Screen and Once-Per-Lifetime Bundling Node'. Its text: 'Section 61-11-26(o) by its terms reaches only §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a, and neither § 60A-4-407 nor § 17C-5-2b cross-references it; both were read in full at source on 2026-08-06 and neither contains a limit referring to § 61-11-26. The textual reading is therefore that they are separate limits in separate statutes, but a participant deciding whether to spend their one lifetime petition needs a settled answer rather than a textual reading.'
theOpenCounselQuestionIWasAskedToRecordN.isItAListedExclusionForBothMyFamilies: YES, confirmed for both. Each track's own exclusions array in the registry carries 'A person who has already obtained expungement under § 61-11-26 or § 61-11-26a. The relief is available only once', and the route census's statuteOrAuthority for each of the two route keys names W. Va. Code § 61-11-26(o) explicitly among its fifteen citations. Both families also defer to wv_common_conv_procedure by name for the fifteen § 61-11-26(c) exclusion subdivisions, so the node carrying the open question is the node they screen against.
theOpenCounselQuestionIWasAskedToRecordN.doesEitherPacketAddressIt: NO — neither one, and this is the answer to what I was asked to check. I searched both participant-instructions.md files in full. Neither contains the phrase once per lifetime, nor 'only once', nor § 61-11-26(o), nor § 17C-5-2b, nor § 60A-4-407, nor any other statement that this relief can be used a single time. A participant is told what to file, where to file it, that it costs $200 plus $100 on grant, and whom to serve among five recipients — and is not told that filing spends a remedy they get once in their life.
theOpenCounselQuestionIWasAskedToRecordN.whyIDidNotScoreItAFailure: It is an open legal question the repository has already flagged as needing counsel, plus a disclosure gap that is not one of the fifteen obligations. MASTER_QUEUE carries legalInputStatus SETTLED with laneReturnLegalHold null for both families, so nothing in the queue currently holds them on it. Recording it, as instructed, rather than answering it or converting it into an obligation failure of my own invention.
theOpenCounselQuestionIWasAskedToRecordN.whyItStillMatters: The two questions compound. The multiple-misdemeanour route is built to put every eligible conviction into one petition precisely because the remedy is once-only, and the same shared node carries a second unanswered question about whether a multi-county group may be venued in the county of residence. The route census's own runtime-authority note says the wrong choice there 'goes to counsel' on 'a once-per-lifetime remedy'. A participant who files a single-misdemeanour petition without being told the relief is once-only may spend it on the smallest thing on their record.
theOpenCounselQuestionIWasAskedToRecordN.relatedFindingInTheSamePair: The eligibility-date defect I scored under REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING has the same consequence class: the instructions ask the participant to choose among four statutory branches the packet has already chosen for them, and a participant who dates the wrong branch swears an eligibility basis inconsistent with the box the packet checked — on a remedy they get once.

forTheCaptain.subject: Utah: the repository holds a $65.00 BCI application fee and both packets deny an amount exists.
forTheCaptain.detail: The instructions say 'this packet does not state an amount because BCI sets it per applicant.' Page 17 of the delivered canonical.pdf prints 'The application fee is $65.00 and non-refundable' and page 18 prints it twice more. There are two BCI money items and the packet conflates them: the $65.00 application fee, fixed and printed on the packet's own paper, and the per-incident certificate price, which genuinely is set per applicant and which the packet is right to refuse. Repair is one sentence. This is the shared Utah host, so it fixes both families at once.

forTheCaptain.subject: Utah dismissed-with-prejudice: a free route the registry says MUST be disclosed before payment is not disclosed.
forTheCaptain.detail: The committed track registry for ut_pet_dismissed_with_prejudice states 'the petition is the faster paid route to the same result and THE FREE ROUTE MUST BE DISCLOSED BEFORE PAYMENT' — automatic expungement under 77-40a-206, 180 days after dismissal. The packet is byte-identical to its conviction sibling's, which has no free alternative, and discloses nothing. It sends the participant to pay $150 plus $65 plus certificate fees for a result the repository says arrives free. Sharing one instruction file across the two routes is what erased the difference; the repair is per-route instructions on the shared host.

forTheCaptain.subject: Utah: the repository and the official source disagree on who serves the prosecutor.
forTheCaptain.detail: The committed track registry, the route census and the packet-set manifest all say the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney and the petitioner does not serve. The held official BCI Expungement Applicant Instructions — which I rehashed to 9e03980f… and extracted — head Step 2 'File the petition with the court and serve the Prosecutor' and say 'Mail or email the prosecutor copies of what you file.' The packet followed the official source, which under AGENTS.md's source hierarchy is correct and is also the safer instruction. I scored SERVICE a PASS and left the three records alone. This is a registry, census and manifest fidelity repair shared across the Utah families and their siblings, not a packet repair.

forTheCaptain.subject: West Virginia: neither packet tells the participant the relief is once per lifetime.

The once-only bar is a listed exclusion on both tracks and § 61-11-26(o) is named in each route's statuteOrAuthority, and neither packet mentions it. Whether the disclosure belongs in the packet is a counsel call. The open 17C-5-2b question sits behind it and is unanswered.

forTheCaptain.subject: West Virginia: one shared instruction fix closes both families.
forTheCaptain.detail: The eligibility-date bullet is byte-identical in both and both are built by the same host, build-census-v1-ne-setaside-custodial-set.mjs. It names four AcroForm field ids where each family's own field map declares exactly one required and refuses the other three by route, asks the participant to determine 'the selected statutory route' the packet already selected without saying which, and carries the WVSCA's own 'Felony' naming and the misspelling MulitipleFelonlySatisfiesDate into participant-facing copy on a misdemeanour-only petition. One line per family.

forTheCaptain.subject: Arkansas: the family's own queue row says its sources are not exactly bound.
forTheCaptain.detail: MASTER_QUEUE carries sourceStatus SOURCE_IDENTITY_NOT_EXACT with sourceReadiness.ready false and boundCount 0 of 2, because the census names the forms official-form:ACIC-PETITION-TO-SEAL-ARREST while the corpus index registers the same bytes as AR-ACIC-PETITION-TO-SEAL-ARREST-UNDER-ACT-1460, so the exact-form-number resolver falls back to a token-subset heuristic. The bytes are exact and provably the named forms and I scored SOURCE_IDENTITY a PASS on that basis, but no route should be promoted while its own queue row says its sources are not exactly bound. The repair is an identifier alias in the source registry, not a rebuild.

forTheCaptain.subject: Sweep A2 by pattern, not by instance.
forTheCaptain.detail: ar-arrest-seal-set was repaired for the one A2 instance a lane reported, and I found two more of exactly the same shape on the same family: FILING_DESTINATION defers to the circuit clerk for a venue three held records establish, and SERVICE affirmatively denies a deadline the packet-set manifest sets at three days. It may be worth asking, for every family A2 named and for each of the three obligations, whether the packet defers to an authority on something the compiled profile, the track registry, the route census or the packet-set manifest already answers — rather than repairing the reported sentence.
